text:
Brandon Montour is Seattle's minutes leader on defense at more than 24 a night, with 12 points in 15 games. He has been the tone setter, as Alison Lukan put it after the overtime win over Calgary, playing 30 minutes twice and joining the rush the way he did in Florida, where he won a Stanley Cup in 2024.

The numbers say the points are running hot. The Kraken have scored 5.2 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, his own shooting (11%) is well above a defenseman's norm, and his points per 60 sit above his usual range. That is why our numbers flag him as due to cool.

The good news is that his game holds up relative to the team: Seattle is 6.5 points better in expected goals share with him than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the better setup men on defense last season, with 31% of his shots coming off the rush. Evolving-Hockey had him better by expected wins than by actual goals last year. The role is solid; the scoring pace is the part to discount.
headline: Montour logs the minutes, and the bounces are helping
